en.title: Partition into Equal-Length Subsequences with Distinct Values
en.description:
Put every array element into exactly one subsequence of length k so that the values within each group are pairwise distinct; subsequences keep the original index order but need not be contiguous.

This site independently prepared the standard I/O and the solution; supplements for bounds missing from the source and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n k, and the second line contains n integers. OCR004 gives the definition and 005 completes the original bounds: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤k≤n, 1≤a[i]≤100000.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: Yes; No; Yes. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Check that n is divisible by k and that no value occurs more times than the number of groups n/k.
